description: The chart, Figure 8, represents the problem distribution based on correctness under two settings: with knowledge and without knowledge, using Zero-Shot. The chart consists of three pie charts, each divided into four slices. The three pie charts are labeled "easy", "medium", and "hard", and each has four categories: N+K+, N+K-, N-K+, and N-K-, represented by different colors, with a legend provided to the right of the "hard" chart. The "easy" chart has N+K+ at approximately 55.4%, N-K+ at around 38.3%, N-K- at about 4.7% with N+K- not visible, and a small unlabeled section. The "medium" chart has N+K+ at around 58.8%, N-K+ at approximately 35.4%, N-K- at about 4.8% with N+K- not visible. The "hard" chart has N-K+ at around 37.9%, N+K- at approximately 37.3%, N-K- at about 18.1%, and N+K+ at 6.7%. The charts are visually distinct, with the "easy" and "medium" charts having one slice much smaller than the others, while the "hard" chart has more evenly distributed slices. The percentage labels are shown inside each slice.
